steps.title: Game and herbs
steps.body: Mourvèdre's gamey, herbal style suits Provençal and Mediterranean food: lamb with rosemary, beef daube, game, wild boar, grilled sausages. Bandol rosé is a classic with bouillabaisse, Marseille's fish stew. Spanish Monastrell suits roast lamb, chorizo and hearty stews.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve reds at 16 to 18 degrees. Young Bandol can be closed and reductive; decant it for an hour or two. Good Bandol ages 15 to 25 years, gaining leather, truffle and dried herbs. Most Spanish Monastrell is best within five years; premium examples age longer.

steps.prompt: Which dish is a classic partner for Bandol rosé?
steps.explanation: Bandol rosé's structure suits the rich, saffron-scented fish stew of Marseille.

steps.body: If a young Mourvèdre smells of struck match, give it time in a decanter. That reductive note usually fades, revealing fruit and herbs.

steps.prompt: Good Bandol red can age for 15 to 25 years.
steps.explanation: Yes. Mourvèdre's tannin and resistance to oxidation help it age.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Mourvèdre suits lamb, game and Provençal dishes
Decant young Bandol; serve at 16 to 18 degrees
